title: Multiplayer DNA Double Helix Unzip
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D educational simulation of DNA double helix unzipping using Three.js in a single HTML file. The scene simulates two players collaborating to unzip a DNA strand by each controlling a helicase enzyme from opposite ends.

## Scene Setup
- Background: dark navy (#0a0a2e) with subtle particle stars for a microscopic environment feel.
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 20), looking at origin, FOV 60.
- Lighting: Ambient light (intensity 0.3, color #4466aa), two directional lights from upper-left and upper-right (intensity 0.8 each, white).
- OrbitControls enabled but with damping, minDistance 10, maxDistance 40.

## DNA Double Helix Structure
- Build a DNA double helix with exactly 20 base pairs along the Y-axis, centered at origin.
- Each strand is a series of spheres (radius 0.3) connected by thin cylinders (backbone).
- Strand A (left): colored blue (#3366ff) spheres.
- Strand B (right): colored red (#ff3366) spheres.
- Base pairs are horizontal cylinders (radius 0.08, colored green #33ff66 for G-C pairs and yellow #ffff33 for A-T pairs) connecting corresponding spheres on each strand.
- The helix should have a twist: each base pair is rotated 36 degrees around the Y-axis from the previous one, with vertical spacing of 0.34 units (matching real DNA proportions scaled up).
- Base pair indices go from 0 (bottom) to 19 (top).

## Helicase Enzymes (Player Avatars)
- Player 1 helicase: a glowing cyan (#00ffff) torus (radius 0.8, tube 0.2) starting at base pair index 0 (bottom).
- Player 2 helicase: a glowing magenta (#ff00ff) torus (radius 0.8, tube 0.2) starting at base pair index 19 (top).
- Each helicase sits at the Y-position of its current base pair and is oriented to face along the helix axis.

## Unzipping Mechanics
- Player 1 presses 'W' to advance their helicase upward (from base pair 0 toward 19).
- Player 2 presses 'ArrowUp' to advance their helicase downward (from base pair 19 toward 0).
- When a helicase arrives at a base pair, that base pair begins an unzip animation over 500ms: the connecting cylinder scales to 0 on X, then is removed; the two strand spheres at that index move apart by 2 units on the X-axis (left strand goes -2, right strand goes +2). The backbone cylinders adjacent to unzipped pairs should stretch accordingly.
- A helicase can only advance once the current base pair's unzip animation is complete.
- Each advance takes a 300ms cooldown after the unzip completes before next input is accepted.
- Players CANNOT pass through each other. If both helicases would occupy the same base pair or cross, they stop. The meeting point is when Player1.currentIndex >= Player2.currentIndex - 1.
- When they meet (adjacent or same index), trigger a 'fully unzipped' celebration: both strands glow brighter, particles burst from the meeting point.

## Scoring & HUD
- Create a DOM overlay HUD:
  - Top-left: 'Player 1 (Cyan): Base X/20 unzipped' with cyan text.
  - Top-right: 'Player 2 (Magenta): Base X/20 unzipped' with magenta text.
  - Center-top: 'Total Unzipped: X/20' in white, large font.
  - A 'Reset' button at bottom-center that resets the entire simulation.
  - A 'Speed: Normal' toggle button that cycles through Normal (500ms unzip) / Fast (250ms) / Slow (1000ms) modes.
  - Bottom-left: 'Base Pair Legend' showing G-C (green) and A-T (yellow) color coding.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- `totalBasePairs`: 20 (constant)
- `player1Index`: current base pair index of Player 1 helicase (starts at -1, meaning before first pair; goes to 0 when first pair is unzipped)
- `player2Index`: current base pair index of Player 2 helicase (starts at 20, meaning after last pair; goes to 19 when first pair is unzipped)
- `player1Unzipped`: count of base pairs unzipped by Player 1
- `player2Unzipped`: count of base pairs unzipped by Player 2
- `totalUnzipped`: total count of unzipped base pairs
- `unzippedPairs`: array of booleans, length 20, true if that base pair is unzipped
- `player1Animating`: boolean, true while Player 1's unzip animation is in progress
- `player2Animating`: boolean, true while Player 2's unzip animation is in progress
- `fullyUnzipped`: boolean, true when all reachable pairs are unzipped and helicases have met
- `speedMode`: string, one of 'normal', 'fast', 'slow'
- `helixRotationPerPair`: 36 (degrees, constant)
- `verticalSpacing`: 0.34 (units, constant)
- `player1Position`: {x, y, z} of Player 1 helicase mesh
- `player2Position`: {x, y, z} of Player 2 helicase mesh
- `resetCount`: number of times reset has been pressed (starts at 0)
- `basePairTypes`: array of 20 strings, each 'GC' or 'AT', randomly assigned at init (roughly 50/50)

## Animation Loop
- The intact portions of the helix should slowly rotate around the Y-axis (0.2 rad/s) for visual appeal.
- Unzipped strand segments should gently oscillate (sine wave, amplitude 0.3, frequency 1Hz) to simulate freed strand movement.
- Helicase toruses should spin around their own axis continuously (1 rad/s).

## Technical Requirements
- All in one HTML file, use Three.js from CDN (r150+).
- Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop.
- Ensure no NaN values in any position or state variable.
- The scene must be responsive to window resize.
physics_constraints: Base pairs unzip sequentially from each end toward the middle. Helicases cannot cross each other. Unzip animation must complete before next advance. Strand separation distance is exactly 2 units per side from center. Helix geometry follows 36°/pair twist and 0.34 unit vertical spacing.
